options.content:
Use this dashboard from top to bottom. First select `model`, then check User Health to see whether clients are protected. Next use reason-preserving panels to identify the largest failure or policy reason. Then narrow `reason`, `participant_key`, or `escrow_id` and inspect participant quality, skipped slots, timeout work, and gateway mechanics.

Every failure panel keeps the bounded `reason` label. A panel that shows only failed volume is paired with a reason or visibility breakdown. Rows marked diagnostic use existing gateway or host metrics that are useful for operations but do not replace the participant-quality score.

Empty data usually means Prometheus cannot scrape `devshard-gateway`, the gateway image predates these metrics, or no `/v1/chat/completions` traffic hit the selected time range.

panels.description: 1 means Prometheus can scrape the gateway. 0 or no data means the rest of this dashboard is not trustworthy yet.
panels.title: Gateway Scrape

panels.description: Total gateway request rate for the selected model. This is the denominator for the request-level ratios in this row.
panels.title: User Request Rate

panels.description: Successful or cached user requests divided by all gateway requests for the selected model.
panels.title: User Success Rate

panels.description: User-visible failures that should stay near zero. Drill into the adjacent reason panel before changing protocol parameters.
panels.title: Critical User Failure Rate

panels.description: Cached requests divided by all gateway requests. A high value means users are protected by cached output, but winner attribution may be incomplete.
panels.title: Cache Hit Share

panels.description: Final user outcomes grouped by bounded reason. Use this to decide whether user-visible problems are transport, policy, runtime, or request-shape issues.
panels.title: What Users Saw by Outcome and Reason

panels.description: Top user-visible failure reasons in the selected range. Pick one of these in `reason` before inspecting participant and slot rows.
panels.title: Top User-Visible Failure Reasons

panels.description: Gateway route p95 from the existing HTTP histogram. This is not model-aware; use it as a route diagnostic only.
panels.title: Gateway Route p95

panels.description: Gateway-wide and participant-budget rejections. A high value means requests are blocked before useful participant work begins.
panels.title: Admission Rejections by Reason

panels.description: Current limiter load and effective caps after capacity scaling. Rising in-flight values near caps explain gateway-limited outcomes.
panels.title: Active Requests and Input Tokens

panels.description: Real upstream sends by role and reason. Extra attempts are the immediate cost of redundancy and fallback.
panels.title: Real Attempts Started by Role and Reason

panels.description: How real attempts terminated. Visibility separates user-visible winners, suppressed losers, no-winner attempts, and unfinished failures.
panels.title: Terminal Attempts by Outcome and Visibility

panels.description: Failed attempts with reason and visibility preserved. Select a high-volume reason before moving to Participant Quality.
panels.title: Failed Attempts by Reason and Visibility

panels.description: Participants whose output users actually saw. Cached requests are excluded unless the gateway can safely attribute the source winner.
panels.title: Top User-Visible Winners

panels.description: Real sends divided by user requests. Values above 1 mean redundancy or recovery is spending extra participant work.
panels.title: Sent Attempts per User Request

panels.description: Failed or not-finished sent attempts divided by successful user requests. This shows work hidden from clients by redundancy.
panels.title: Failed Sent Attempts per Successful Request

panels.description: Diagnostic only: receipt p95 is keyed by escrow-local `host_idx`, not participant key. Use it for timeout-window tuning, not participant scoring.
panels.title: Diagnostic Receipt p95 by Escrow Host

panels.description: Diagnostic only: first-token p95 is host-index based. Future participant-key first-content metrics will replace this for participant quality.
panels.title: Diagnostic First Token p95 by Escrow Host

panels.description: Diagnostic only: prefill time per input token by escrow-local host index. Do not compare this directly with participant-key failure rates.
panels.title: Diagnostic CTTFL per Input Token p95

panels.description: Diagnostic only: total attempt time by escrow-local host index. Use with timeout rows to tune windows.
panels.title: Diagnostic Total Attempt Time p95

panels.description: Successful user requests that hid participant or policy failures. Severity separates protected pre-winner failures from later winner problems.
panels.title: Hidden User Successes by Severity and Reason

panels.description: Suppressed loser failures by reason. These did not reach the user but still consumed participant work.
panels.title: Hidden Loser Failures by Reason

panels.description: User-visible winner attempts that also recorded a failure reason. Investigate these first because users may have seen partial content or degraded streams.
panels.title: Winner Failures After User-Visible Content

panels.description: Participant drilldown for the selected reason. This is the main path from a top reason to specific addresses.
panels.title: Participants for Selected Failure Reason

panels.description: Extra real sends divided by all user requests. This is direct redundancy cost.
panels.title: Extra Real Sends per User Request

panels.description: No-send or skipped slot burns divided by user requests. This captures scheduling cost before HTTP send.
panels.title: Ghost or No-Send Slots per User Request

panels.description: Suppressed loser terminal attempts divided by user requests. This shows completed work not shown to the user.
panels.title: Suppressed Losers per User Request

panels.description: Extra-attempt reasons that are expected to protect users. High values can justify redundancy but should still guide timeout tuning.
panels.title: Useful Redundancy Reasons

panels.description: Exploration-driven extra attempts. Use this to separate protocol learning cost from failure recovery cost.
panels.title: Exploration Extra Attempts

panels.description: No-send reasons that indicate policy pressure, capability mismatch, or participant health problems rather than useful recovery.
panels.title: Waste or Policy Pressure No-Sends

panels.description: Skipped/no-send slots by participant, model, escrow, reason, and quarantine mode. This answers which scheduling changes happened before any HTTP send.

targets.expr: topk(30, sum(increase(devshard_gateway_slot_decisions_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",escrow_id=~"$escrow_id",reason=~"$reason",decision!="real_send"}[$__range])) by (participant_key, model, escrow_id, reason, quarantine_mode))

panels.title: Skipped Slots by Participant, Model, Escrow, and Reason

panels.description: Current probe, shadow, probation, or manual no-winner state. A value of 1 means the participant is currently in that mode.
panels.title: Current Quarantine or No-Winner State

panels.description: Quarantine and no-winner transitions by reason. Use this to find participants entering probe, shadow, probation, or manual suspicion.
panels.title: Quarantine Transitions by Participant and Reason

panels.description: Real no-winner sends by reason and quarantine mode. These participants help availability but should not win unless no clean winner exists.
panels.title: No-Winner Attempts by Reason and Mode

panels.description: Escrows blocked by participant budgets. Use with skipped-slot rows to determine whether pressure is participant-local or escrow-local.
panels.title: Escrow Participant Budget Pressure

panels.description: Participants with at least `min_attempts` real sends in the selected range. This is the base volume filter for the quality row.

targets.expr: topk(30, sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Sent Attempts by Participant and Model

panels.description: Successful terminal attempts divided by all terminal attempts for participants above the volume threshold.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_terminal_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",outcome="success"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_terminal_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Participant Success Rate

panels.description: Selected-reason failures divided by sent attempts for participants above the volume threshold.

targets.expr: topk(30, (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1)) and on (participant_key, model) (sum by (participant_key, model) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])) >= $min_attempts))

panels.title: Selected-Reason Failure Rate

panels.description: No-receipt and empty-stream rates by participant. These are common quarantine inputs.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~"no_receipt|empty_stream"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1))

panels.title: No-Receipt and Empty-Stream Rates

panels.description: Transport and EOF failure rates by participant. These usually point to upstream connectivity or stream truncation.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempt_failures_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",reason=~".*transport.*|eof.*|error_stream"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (participant_key, model, reason) (increase(devshard_gateway_attempts_started_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model"}[$__range])), 1))

panels.title: Transport and EOF Failure Rates

panels.description: Timeout action pressure, user-visible wins, no-winner attempts, quarantine skips, and current mode. Use this as the quality summary before opening escrow diagnostics.
panels.title: Participant Quality Detail Signals

panels.description: Heatmap-style table of participant x model failures by reason. Sort by value to find model-localized bad addresses.
panels.title: Participant x Model Failure Heatmap

panels.description: Heatmap-style table of participant x escrow skipped slots. This is diagnostic and should not replace the participant+model quality view.
panels.title: Participant x Escrow Skipped-Slot Heatmap

panels.description: Model x escrow ghost/no-send pressure. High values indicate localized routing, capability, or quarantine pressure.
panels.title: Model x Escrow No-Send Pressure

panels.description: Capacity-aware picker choices by model and escrow. Use this to confirm traffic is flowing to expected escrows.
panels.title: Runtime Picker Choices by Model and Escrow

panels.description: Capability no-send skips by model and participant. This uses the existing bounded slot-decision reason, not the future capability-subreason metric.
panels.title: Capability Skips by Model and Participant

panels.description: Timeout work grouped by kind and action. Failed or skipped actions should be understood before tuning timeouts.
panels.title: Expected, Started, Completed, Skipped, or Failed Timeout Work

panels.description: Top timeout skip and failure reasons in the selected range.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum(increase(devshard_gateway_timeout_actions_total{participant_key=~"$participant_key",model=~"$model",action=~"skipped|failed",reason=~"$reason"}[$__range])) by (participant_key, model, kind, action, reason))

panels.title: Timeout Skip and Failure Reasons

panels.description: Terminal attempts that did not finish, shown next to timeout actions. If this rises without timeout work, timeout handling is missing or skipped.
panels.title: Not-Finished Attempts Beside Timeout Work

panels.description: Cache hit and total request rates. This is diagnostic because cache hits may not carry fresh participant attribution.
panels.title: Cache and Request Lifecycle

panels.description: Participant-bound transport errors by path kind and upstream status. Use this before blaming model quality.
panels.title: Upstream Transport Errors

panels.description: Speculative decisions and attempt starts by reason. This explains why the gateway decided to race or explore.
panels.title: Speculative Routing Mechanics

panels.description: Runtime active state, active requests, and reserved tokens by model and escrow. Use this when picker or capacity panels look wrong.
panels.title: Runtime Activity and Reserved Tokens

panels.description: Current capacity scale and weights. Scale is current weight divided by baseline; values below 1 explain lower effective caps.
panels.title: Model Capacity Scale and Weights

panels.description: Host transport connection state by remote address. This is network plumbing evidence, not participant scoring.
panels.title: Host Transport Connections

panels.description: Reasons that create extra sends or hidden failures. Use this to tune redundancy and timeout windows by model.
panels.title: Redundancy Pressure by Reason and Model

panels.description: Participants that repeatedly require extra sends, no-winner handling, or quarantine transitions. These are candidates for incentive and quarantine tuning.
panels.title: Participant Protocol-Tuning Candidates

panels.description: Escrow sizing pressure from model capacity, runtime load, and blocked participants. Use this to decide whether capacity or routing needs adjustment.
panels.title: Escrow Sizing and Capacity Pressure
